chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Fuzayl, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Everything by which a man opens his sustenance, it is trade/business.

key_terms.رِزْق: Sustenance, livelihood, or provision from God

ai.seo_question: What constitutes trade or business in Shia jurisprudence according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) defines the acquisition of livelihood (*rizq*) through any initiated means as *tijarah* (trade/commerce), emphasizing the active role of human effort in sustenance. This broad classification underscores the Islamic principle that all legitimate economic activities, regardless of their specific nature, fall under the ethical and legal framework of commerce, thereby encouraging diligence and integrity in one's professional endeavors.
